endorsements.quote: Use only AI models that have demonstrated impact on patient outcomes, decision-making processes, or risk stratification validated through prospective studies or randomized clinical trials.
Before any AI model can be safely deployed at scale, hospitals and health systems need tools and processes to assess how well these models perform within their specific clinical contexts.
A key early requirement is the establishment of robust local validation infrastructures.
In line with the AI Act, these programs should also ensure traceability, documenting who was trained, by whom, on which tools, and at what competency level.
Healthcare professionals must acquire a digital health literacy level appropriate for their specific role, with individuals with leadership and management roles having more in-depth knowledge.
AI education should be tiered by role and aligned with digital competence levels, from foundational to expert
Additionally, CAIDs play a key role in ongoing model evaluation and recalibration, which is essential as patient characteristics and populations change over time.
The creation of Clinical AI Departments (CAIDs) within healthcare institutions offers a structured approach to managing AI integration [ 13 ].
To overcome these challenges, healthcare institutions must invest in flexible, ongoing AI training programs and formally integrate AI education into medical and specialty training [ 33 ].

unlisted_practices: Digitalize the emergency, critical, and perioperative patient journey by adopting a shared standard structure for electronic medical records optimized for data sharing and interoperability.
Adopt data standards such as HL7 FHIR and FAIR principles to ensure secure, interoperable health data exchange.
Involve clinicians, administrators, patients, and developers in co-designing digital and AI solutions.
Implement a data quality checklist and enhance AI model transparency as recommended by the WHO.
Use federated learning and blockchain as privacy-preserving data-sharing approaches.
Provide financial incentives and strategic investment in digital infrastructure, particularly in under-resourced settings.
Develop robust certification pathways for AI models aligned with the AI Act and Medical Device Regulation.
Leaders should articulate a strategic vision for AI, secure resources, and foster a culture of innovation with iterative implementation.

screen.reason: Expert consensus statement outlining strategic recommendations and priorities for integrating AI safely into emergency, critical, and perioperative medicine.
